title: AnyVIO: Feed-Forward Streaming Visual-Inertial Odometry Across Platforms
summary: Geometric foundation models (GFMs) estimate camera mo- tion and scene structure from images without requiring ex- pert parameter tuning, but either lack metric scale or rely on learned priors to infer scale, which is unobservable from monocular images alone. Inertial sensing offers a way to observe metric scale, but existing methods add inertial in- formation through a filter or factor graph, which reintro- duces bespoke parameter tuning and optimization costs that can grow with the trajectory. To bridge this gap, we present AnyVIO, a real-time, feed-forward streaming model for monocular visual-inertial odometry (VIO), which combines a streaming GFM with an inertial foundation model (IFM). Both the GFM and IFM predict the metric motion between consecutive frames, and a lightweight learned fusion head quantifies the reliability of each estimate and blends them in a single forward pass. Across nine datasets recorded from cars, legged and ground robots, and handheld and head- mounted devices, AnyVIO reduces the metric position error of its visual model by 36% while publishing each pose esti- mate 70 ms after an image is received. We further deploy AnyVIO onboard two real vehicles at up to 140 km/h, where it remains accurate in poor lighting and heavy dust.

title: UHD Low-Light Image Enhancement via Real-Time Enhancement Methods with Clifford Information Fusion
comment: We request to withdraw this manuscript, as we have identified serious data errors in the baseline comparisons and hallucinated citations in the paper. Thank you
summary: Considering efficiency, ultra-high-definition (UHD) low-light image restoration is extremely challenging. Existing methods based on Transformer architectures or high-dimensional complex convolutional neural networks often suffer from the "memory wall" bottleneck, failing to achieve millisecond-level inference on edge devices. To address this issue, we propose a novel real-time UHD low-light enhancement network based on geometric feature fusion using Clifford algebra in 2D Euclidean space. First, we construct a four-layer feature pyramid with gradually increasing resolution, which decomposes input images into low-frequency and high-frequency structural components via a Gaussian blur kernel, and adopts a lightweight U-Net based on depthwise separable convolution for dual-branch feature extraction. Second, to resolve structural information loss and artifacts from traditional high-low frequency feature fusion, we introduce spatially aware Clifford algebra, which maps feature tensors to a multivector space (scalars, vectors, bivectors) and uses Clifford similarity to aggregate features while suppressing noise and preserving textures. In the reconstruction stage, the network outputs adaptive Gamma and Gain maps, which perform physically constrained non-linear brightness adjustment via Retinex theory. Integrated with FP16 mixed-precision computation and dynamic operator fusion, our method achieves millisecond-level inference for 4K/8K images on a single consumer-grade device, while outperforming state-of-the-art (SOTA) models on several restoration metrics.

title: Lightweight Low-Frequency Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring via Karhunen-Loève Feature Distillation and Temporal Convolutional Networks
comment: 10 pages, 6 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid. S. Peeris, P. Thennakoon and P. Sumanasekara contributed equally
summary: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) is a critical enabler for demand-side management which allows for smart grid optimization. A deployment-ready NILM solution necessitates three key features: accurate disaggregation, low-frequency sampling, and low computational cost. This paper proposes a lightweight, edge-oriented NILM framework that combines activity-boundary-aware synthetic data augmentation with Karhunen-Loève Transform (KLT) feature extraction and a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN). The augmentation stage extracts and recombines complete or near-complete appliance activation segments so that the model can be trained without new fully labeled household aggregates. The KLT filter bank extracts decorrelated, appliance-informed temporal features which are then fed into a compact TCN along with the original aggregate for energy disaggregation. Evaluations on two standard NILM datasets, UK-DALE and REDD, at 10-s sampling and with leave-one-house-out testing, demonstrate that the proposed architecture achieves comparable or superior disaggregation accuracy relative to NILMFormer, BERT4NILM, BiLSTM, and BiGRU. The computational footprint of the framework is 31,009 parameters, the fewest of the five models compared, and on a single CPU thread it needs 2.78 ms per 1000 samples, 84-95% less than the baselines. These results demonstrate a favorable accuracy-efficiency tradeoff for low-frequency smart-meter NILM.

title: Accord: Universal Online Metric Localization and Dense Mapping from one Camera and an IMU
summary: Dense metric mapping from a single camera and IMU remains challenging: visual-inertial odometry (VIO) provides metric motion but sparse geometry, whereas feed-forward depth models predict dense structure without ensuring metric scale. We present Accord, which constructs an accurate online dense metric map from any camera with an IMU. A VIO filter publishes metric poses, a depth foundation model conditioned on them predicts depth for short keyframe windows, and a factor graph fuses the resulting submaps. Recent work has explored several approaches to this problem. What is essential is the multi-view agreement (Accord), which is considered in SLAM as a source of geometric self-consistency. Accord anchors each keyframe window to metric 3D points triangulated from the filter poses, then exploits bidirectional dense depth agreement between co-visible images to estimate and correct per-image scale errors while preserving the metric scale established by the anchors. Context keyframes further improve depth prediction, and the resulting submaps are fused in a factor graph. We evaluate a single mapping configuration across five public camera-IMU setups and a new Phone-rig/GoPro dataset. With nothing tuned per dataset/setup and every map aligned only by Accord's own trajectory, Accord achieves consistently best/second-best mean F-score at 5 cm on every platform. Accord is open-source along with the phone-rig dataset for the benefit of the research community

title: A Wolf in Sheep's Pixels: Visual Camouflage Attacks via HDR Gain Maps
summary: An image can pass automated safety checks while showing harmful content to its human viewer. We introduce DRJanus, a visual camouflage attack that exploits the gap between standard dynamic range (SDR) processing and high dynamic range (HDR) display. Automated systems often read only an image's SDR base, whereas HDR viewers reconstruct its appearance using an auxiliary gain map. DRJanus inverts this reconstruction to embed two independently chosen color images in a single JPEG, without querying or optimizing against the target model. It preserves the chosen SDR base exactly and reconstructs HDR targets at an average PSNR of 43.03 dB across 400 images. On a benchmark of 100 sexual-content images, DRJanus evades detection by all six tested commercial moderation services and nine vision-language models. Across five agents, each evaluated on 120 task cases per threat setting, attack success ranges from 31.67% to 100% for moderation evasion and from 95% to 100% for task manipulation. We also explore cross-view consistency checks as a mitigation. These findings expose a gap in visual trust: securing what a machine reads does not secure what a user sees. A demo is available at https://qshen0629.github.io/DRJanus/

title: TuringPAI: A Foundation for On-Device Physical AI
summary: Physical AI requires models that understand spatial relationships and dynamic environments and translate observations into actions under limited onboard compute. We present TuringPAI, a family of models for on-device Physical AI comprising TuringPAI-VL for shared vision-language understanding, TuringPAI-Drive for autonomous driving, and TuringPAI-Embodied for robotic manipulation. TuringPAI-VL is a 0.65B model built on HybridViT-MLQ, which combines convolutional local aggregation with Transformer-based global modeling. Multi-scale Latent Queries integrate spatial features and observation history within the same visual Transformer, providing a compact, structured interface to the language model. Training combines general vision-language data with geometric, cross-view, and temporal supervision. TuringPAI-VL supports general multimodal understanding and improves quantitative geometric perception over Qwen2-VL-2B, while providing a shared initialization for the two downstream VLA models. For autonomous driving, TuringPAI-Drive maintains all evaluated ADE/FDE metrics within 1.2\% of a full-token HybridViT baseline using the MLQ interface and achieves comparable aggregate scores in an in-house simulation evaluation. Using XPeng Native Runtime (XNRT) on a single NVIDIA Orin-X SoC, TuringPAI-Drive generates trajectories at 12\,Hz in on-vehicle operation. For robotic manipulation, TuringPAI-Embodied achieves a 96.8\% average success rate across the four LIBERO suites. These results demonstrate a shared vision-language foundation for driving and robotic manipulation under practical on-device constraints.

title: QFT-Based Hybrid PointNet-Quantum Neural Networks for LiDAR Point-Cloud Classification
summary: Hybrid quantum-classical learning architectures provide a promising framework for integrating quantum feature transformations into complex data-processing tasks. Among these transformations, the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) offers a structured approach to feature processing, motivating an investigation of how its circuit configuration influences predictive performance, quantum resource requirements, and noise robustness. We present a hybrid PointNet-quantum neural network architecture for LiDAR point-cloud classification, combining classical feature extraction, amplitude encoding, and a variational quantum circuit. Five Fourier-processing configurations are systematically evaluated: No-QFT, Full-QFT-After, QFT-no-swap, IQFT-After, and Trainable-QFT. Experiments on KITTI, nuScenes, and PandaSet across three random seeds assess classification performance, class-level behavior, circuit complexity, and sensitivity to the IBM FakeManilaV2 noise model. Under ideal simulation, IQFT-After achieves the highest weighted F1-score on KITTI (0.857 $\pm$ 0.033), compared with 0.838 $\pm$ 0.023 for No-QFT. Removing the final SWAP gates in the QFT circuit reduces circuit complexity while preserving the Pauli-Z measurement features up to a fixed permutation that can be absorbed by the classification head. Under quantum noise, the circuit ranking changes, with IQFT-After exhibiting greater performance degradation and No-QFT and Trainable-QFT showing stronger robustness. Per-class analysis further identifies dataset-dependent differences in minority-class performance. These results demonstrate that Fourier-processing configuration influences both classification behavior and noise sensitivity, highlighting the role of circuit structure and hardware-aware evaluation in hybrid quantum learning for three-dimensional point-cloud data.

title: Multi-View Transformer with Geometry-Guided Multi-Modal ControlNet for 3D Virtual Try-On
summary: Editing a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) capture of a person so that they wear a new garment requires every rendered view to agree on the same garment details. Existing 3D virtual try-on (VTON) pipelines, however, edit training views largely independently and fuse them with hand-designed heuristics such as manually chosen reference views and fixed attention-blending weights. The resulting inconsistencies are baked into the 3D representation and surface as texture drift, blurred prints, and implausible geometry in novel views. We present GS-VTON-MVT, a three-stage framework that combines implicit and explicit 3D reasoning for consistent 3DGS try-on. (i) A multi-view inpainting transformer jointly edits a set of training views with full cross-view self-attention, so that cross-view correspondence is learned rather than imposed. (ii) A geometry-guided multi-modal ControlNet conditions the diffusion editor on the garment image together with depth and surface normals rendered from the current 3DGS state, supplying explicit structure where visual evidence is weakest. (iii) A pose-adaptive persona-aware attention replaces the fixed blending weight between current-view and reference-view features with weights derived from camera-pose proximity. On the 3D-VTONBench benchmark, GS-VTON-MVT improves FID, KID, LPIPS-based cross-view consistency, and user preference over general-purpose 3D editors and prior 3D try-on methods.

title: Stereo Visual Odometry with In-the-Loop Geometric Feed-Forward Models Towards Dense Metric Mapping
summary: We present a stereo visual odometry (SVO) framework that integrates geometric feed-forward models (GFMs) for dense depth prediction with factor-graph-based visual odometry to achieve accurate localisation and dense metric mapping. Our key idea is to exploit sparse but reliable metric geometry estimated from stereo and temporal multi-view observations to calibrate dense GFM predictions, while retaining the robustness and efficiency of model-based SVO. Rather than directly conditioning the GFM on potentially noisy stereo depth, optimised 3D landmarks are used to jointly estimate a scale-shift transformation over all keyframes within each local submap, yielding metrically consistent dense depth predictions. To balance accuracy and computational efficiency, we introduce a hierarchical factor-graph architecture. At the local level, sliding-window optimisation estimates high-frequency camera poses and multi-view-refined 3D landmarks. Dense predictions are generated only for selected keyframes and registered within each submap using SE(3) Generalised ICP. Consecutive submaps are further aligned in Sim(3) using their shared geometry, allowing residual scale inconsistencies to be corrected. These intra- and inter-submap constraints are incorporated into a global factor graph to produce a consistent trajectory and dense metric reconstruction. Extensive experiments on public and in-house datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves competitive odometry accuracy against geometric and learning-based baselines while providing accurate dense metric reconstruction and improved robustness to failures in learned depth prediction.

title: Learning-Based System Identification for DVL-Constrained AUV Localization
summary: Nowadays, most AUVs utilize Doppler velocity logs (DVLs) and inertial measurement units (IMUs) to achieve satisfactory dead-reckoning results. However, the DVL bottom lock may not be available in some scenarios, such as moving over a soft bottom or traveling further away from the seafloor beyond the DVL's range. As a result, the localization system solely reliant on the IMU data will experience significant drift. The relatively high cost of DVLs also inhibits multirobot or swarm operations. In this article, we present the results of using fully connected feedforward neural networks to predict vehicle velocity (surge, sway, and heave) for AUV localization. Approximation functions for the vehicle velocities are derived based on the generalized six degree-of-freedom dynamic equation and kinematics, proving that they are suitable for feedforward neural networks with measurable inputs. The neural networks are trained using field data collected using an AUV. An ablation study was conducted to investigate the impacts of hyperparameters, and the most effective models were selected using the Akaike information criterion. The selected neural network models are tested on three new sets of mission data collected on two different days. The quantitative results show that localization using vehicle velocities predicted by neural networks yields lower averaged root-mean-square distance errors and standard deviation compared to the DVL-aided dead-reckoning method. However, the extent of this improvement was found to depend on ocean current conditions. The promising results show that lightweight fully connected feedforward neural networks offer an attractive approach for inertial-based underwater localization when DVLs or their measurements are not available.

title: From Sequence to Space: Explicit Spatial Belief with Vision-Language Distillation for Active Geo-Localization
summary: Active geo-localization (AGL) asks an agent to navigate a small aerial search grid and reach a target specified by an aerial image, a ground-level photograph, or text. Existing methods align the goal modalities well, but they keep the navigation state inside a large sequential Transformer and train with a dense distance reward that uses the hidden goal location. This paper proposes EAGLE, an Explicit spatial-belief Agent for Geo-Localization and Exploration. Offline training jointly optimizes a teacher-conditioned Swin branch and a context-free Swin student from the same randomly masked partial mosaics. The teacher branch attends to frozen full-scene context extracted by Qwen2.5-VL-7B, both branches receive masked-cell aerial-feature reconstruction and uncertainty supervision, while the student additionally distills stop-gradient feature predictions from the teacher. After distillation, Qwen, its cached context, and the teacher-attention branch are discarded. The retained student predicts cell-level aerial-feature embeddings and predictive uncertainty from partial observations alone. These predictions are combined with the modality-aligned goal embedding and a trajectory-derived visitation mask to construct the spatial belief tensor. The student is then frozen while a compact CNN actor-critic is optimized with PPO. EAGLE achieves state-of-the-art average success rates of 78.1%, 76.4%, and 76.8% on MASA, xBD zero-shot transfer, and the MM-GAG zero-shot aerial-goal split, respectively, without using a VLM or cached visual tokens at inference. Code will be made publicly available.

title: Reference-Twist-Based Velocity-Domain Spatiotemporal Calibration for mmWave Radar, Event Camera, and IMU
summary: Multi-sensor navigation requires a common spatial and temporal basis, but geometric calibration relies on targets, features, point clouds, or pose associations that are difficult to establish across mmWave radars, event cameras, and inertial measurement units (IMUs). These sensors nevertheless share rigid-body motion. This paper formulates reference-conditioned velocity-domain spatiotemporal calibration for a rigid suite of two mmWave radars, one event camera, and two IMUs. Given a trusted reference body twist, radar Doppler, event normal flow, and inertial measurements are regressed against the same motion to estimate relative rotations, lever arms, time offsets, and sensor-specific bias and scale without artificial targets, structure from motion, or cross-modal point-cloud registration. The reference is treated as a conditioning input rather than a sensor to be calibrated. We compare joint and reference- conditioned estimation, derive conditional identifiability and CRLB-level covariance and bias bounds, and state the operating conditions under which conditioning is informative. Indoor and forest recordings with axis-separated motion evaluate initial- ization, temporal alignment, motion degeneracy, reference-input sensitivity, and residual consistency. Because the reference does not add physical observability, the estimates remain conditional on reference accuracy, synchronization, motion excitation, and projection diversity.

title: A Practical Proprioceptive Data Collection Utility for the Unitree GO1
summary: The Unitree Go1 is a widely used platform for legged robotics research, yet collecting proprioceptive data from it is unnecessarily difficult: the Unitree SDK is sparsely documented, and ROS1 (Robot Operating System), the Go1's native middleware, is fully deprecated. We present an open-source graphical utility that enables researchers to reliably record proprioceptive data from the Go1, including joint states, IMU (Inertial Measurement Unit) readings, foot force sensor data, and gyroscope measurements, without requiring ROS expertise. The tool provides a simple GUI (Graphical User Interface) for starting, stopping, and labeling recordings in real time. The contribution of this paper is the collection utility. We characterize the acquisition quality of 51 recordings collected with it, including the achieved sampling rate and repeated samples. As a secondary, deliberately modest check that the data is useful, we train a terrain classifier on it. The results are weak: a Temporal Convolutional Network reaches about 38% accuracy on held-out recordings across ten terrain classes (10% would be chance), and a window-level split that ignores recording boundaries inflates the same measurement to about 99%. We report this as a demonstration that the logged signals carry terrain information, not as a competitive classifier. The utility is designed to lower the barrier to collecting Go1 proprioceptive data without ROS.

title: I See You: Initial Multi-Robot LiDAR Registration with Mutual-Observation Checks
comment: Accepted final version. IEEE International Symposium on Safety, Security, and Rescue Robotics (SSRR), Incheon, South Korea, November 2026. Project page: https://tu-darmstadt-ros-pkg.github.io/i-see-you-registration
summary: Compared to single-robot deployments, multi-robot teams can significantly improve search-and-rescue (SAR) mission success by covering large areas in parallel. To collaborate effectively, these robots must be registered in a common reference frame. Standard registration methods typically rely on external infrastructure or significant map overlap, but real deployments require infrastructure-free, stationary initial alignment for immediate operation. While global LiDAR point cloud registration addresses this, existing single-scan methods often fail silently in aliased or degenerate environments. Approaches scaling beyond two agents also remain rarely evaluated in real-world scenarios. We propose a centralized, deployment-ready framework for pre-mission multi-robot registration. Our system performs pairwise coarse-to-fine alignment and actively rejects impossible pose hypotheses via deterministic plausibility checks. We validate the framework on a real-world custom dataset of four synchronized robots in various environments with ground truth. The checks reject more than a third of the incorrect pairwise registrations while falsely rejecting less than 1% of the correct ones, and reduce the number of team registrations with a wrong robot pose by 38%. Dataset and code are publicly available.

title: SixthSense: Proprioception-Only Whole-Body Wrench Estimation for Humanoids
summary: Humanoid robots are entering the physical world at scale, yet are often criticized as oversized toys---good at dancing, but lacking the force-interaction capabilities for practical tasks. Reliable whole-body contact perception is difficult because floating-base dynamics make proprioceptive wrench recovery ambiguous, while model-based estimators require accurate dynamics and support-force inputs. We propose SixthSense, which uses conditional flow matching to model sparse spatiotemporal fields of link-wise contact gates and 6-D wrenches conditioned on proprioceptive and IMU histories. We train one estimator on pooled data from lying, standing, walking, and motion tracking. Across extensive simulation experiments, SixthSense outperforms learned and model-based baselines in overall contact estimation and remains robust to observation noise. We further establish a real-robot benchmark with our newly collected Unitree G1 dataset, where SixthSense achieves the strongest overall performance among learned estimators and requires approximately 50\,ms per inference. Controlled ambiguity experiments show that its samples recover multiple dynamically plausible contact modes with improved local physical consistency. We finally deploy SixthSense for collision detection and contact-triggered physical human--robot interaction.

title: When Does Cross-View Consistency Matter in Multi-View Appearance Augmentation? A Controlled Study for Visuomotor Policies
summary: Multi-view visual augmentation often seeks consistency across cameras, but it is unclear which forms of consistency matter for downstream control. We use simulation-state replay to manipulate cross-view coupling while preserving the per-camera perturbation distributions, physical trajectories, and action labels. Across seven LIBERO manipulation tasks, marginal-matched changes in global appearance, ghost injection, and target color have small average costs for a late-fusion Diffusion Policy: point estimates are near zero or negative, and the largest upper endpoint of the 90% posterior credible intervals is 2.55 percentage points. In contrast, geometrically anti-coupled observations reduce success by 3.30 percentage points relative to coupled observations (90% CrI [0.64, 6.28]), with displacement magnitude, direction marginals, and the number of affected views matched. Camera interventions reveal substantial dependence on wrist-view geometry, while feature analysis shows appearance sensitivity patterns associated with the factors randomized during training. ACT shows a higher target-color cost estimate than DP, with uncertainty that includes zero and sensitivity to task composition. Within the tested tasks and policy configurations, these findings motivate selective consistency constraints: appearance coupling can sometimes be relaxed, whereas task-relevant geometry and cross-view spatial correspondence warrant protection.

title: SGAR: Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction via Sparse Geometry-Guided Attention
summary: Feed-forward models have been very successful in 3D reconstruction with ad hoc attention designs that relate all view patches densely. However, the cost of this dense global attention grows quadratically with the number of views, preventing the model from applying to larger-scale reconstruction settings. In this paper, we argue that most dense attention computations are unnecessary from a classical structure-from-motion perspective: 3D structures stem from geometrically matching regions in 2D. We bring this principle to learning-based feed-forward reconstruction with our Sparse Geometric Attention Reconstruction (SGAR) method. In SGAR, each patch token attends to only a small set of patch tokens from other views, chosen by a lightweight learned key selection module trained to predict cross-view 3D proximity of tokens. Thus, dense global attention is replaced by much more efficient geometric-similarity-guided sparse attention. SGAR is a general method that can be applied to different feed-forward models by fine-tuning. In our experiments, we show that SGAR is the fastest among both state-of-the-art dense and sparse methods and the most accurate sparse one. It runs up to 12-times faster than dense attention at 1,000 views with stable pose accuracy where existing sparse methods fail, and shows the best performance in reconstructing more complete geometries on the same time budget.

title: Interpretable Prototype-Conditioned Adaptation for Weather Forecasting
comment: 38 pages, including supplementary material. Project page: https://zhixuanli.github.io/projects/li2026protocast
summary: Data-driven weather forecasting requires distinguishing local states and their temporal evolution. However, learned patterns remain implicit in neural forecasters, making their influence difficult to interpret. Failing to distinguish local evolution can lead to similar forecasts for locations that develop differently, increasing prediction error. This motivates explicit references for distinguishing and interpreting local patterns. Prototypes provide explicit pattern references, but sample- or task-level conditioning leaves open how to adapt to distinct locations and variable groups. To deal with this problem, we design ProtoCast, which uses group-specific prototype banks to adapt local features while accounting for cross-variable dependencies. Specifically, (1) we combine each group's historical features and temporal change with forecast context from cross-variable attention for evolution-aware prototype matching. (2) Sparse mixtures of prototype-specific low-rank operators tailor corrections to each group and location. A gated attention block then exchanges the corrected features across groups before prediction. Each group's correction decomposes into explicit prototype contributions before this fusion. (3) We jointly train the forecasting network and operators from scratch and refit each group's prototypes before every training epoch. Slot tracking preserves prototype-operator associations, making each prototype's contribution to local corrections more interpretable. Experiments on GlobalForecast and TyphoonTracking show improved forecasting accuracy, while prototype deletion links local feature contributions to changes in prediction error. This work advances the development of more accurate and interpretable data-driven weather forecasting models. Project page: https://zhixuanli.github.io/projects/li2026protocast

title: Bridging Supervision Gaps: A Unified Framework for Remote Sensing Change Detection
summary: Change detection (CD) identifies surface changes from bi-temporal remote sensing imagery. Depending on annotation budgets and application contexts, real-world change labels take heterogeneous forms: pixel-level masks, image-level labels, unlabeled samples, or mixtures of these supervision types. However, most existing CD methods target a single supervision paradigm and cannot leverage complex annotation scenarios. To tackle this challenge, we present UniCD, a unified change detection framework that accommodates supervised, weakly supervised, unsupervised, and mixed-supervision learning within a single network. To bridge supervision granularity gaps, we design Supervision-Anchored Cross-Granularity Prototype Propagation, which constructs class-specific prototypes from pixel-level annotations and transfers reliable change semantics to image-level labeled and unlabeled samples. We further design Multi-source Consistency Rectification to filter unreliable pseudo labels and selectively recover informative pixels through multi-source evidence and cross-view consistency. Experiments on LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and CLCD demonstrate that UniCD consistently outperforms conventional mixed training, improving the average IoU by 3.02 percentage points across different mixed-supervision settings, while achieving state-of-the-art performance under individual supervision settings.

title: GeoMetric: Injecting Metric Geographic Structure into Worldwide Image Geo-Localization
summary: Worldwide image geo-localization estimates where a photograph was taken on Earth. Existing methods infer location from visual appearance alone, an unreliable cue for geography: near-identical scenes occur on different continents. We present GeoMetric, a three-phase retrieval framework that encodes geographic distance directly in the representation. Phase I trains image, text, and location encoders into a unit hypersphere. The location encoder combines ScaleFusion and GeoAnchorAttention. ScaleFusion projects a coordinate onto an equal-area chart and encodes it with three Fourier bands, fusing them by attention into one multi-scale embedding. GeoAnchorAttention adds a global prior from fixed spherical anchors without mixing samples, so each coordinate embedding is batch-independent. A trimodal contrastive objective aligns images, reverse-geocoded texts, and coordinates, masking semantic and geographic false negatives. Phase II retrieves candidates, each carrying a GPS coordinate and granularity-aware geographic text. Phase III lets a frozen open-source 8B-parameter large multimodal model (LMM) choose the coordinate from those candidates. On four benchmarks, GeoMetric is best in 15 of 20 threshold cells, and ablations show that the components act at different scales: the text encoder carries coarse geographic context, while the location encoder resolves fine-grained distinctions.

title: From Keypoints to Predictive Distributions: Post-Hoc Uncertainty for YOLO-Pose Models
summary: YOLO-Pose models provide efficient multi-object keypoint localization, but do not quantify the associated spatial uncertainty. We introduce a lightweight post-hoc probabilistic extension that augments a trained YOLO-Pose model with calibrated bivariate predictive distributions over keypoint locations, centered at the model's original predictions. Concretely, we train additional probabilistic heads with an importance-weighted negative log-likelihood to predict an input-dependent $2\times2$ dispersion matrix for each keypoint, followed by Gaussian calibration for broad downstream compatibility or Student-$t$ calibration for distributional fidelity. Complementing this, we propose an evaluation protocol that combines a suite of distributional calibration diagnostics with average keypoint precision (AKP), a keypoint-level extension of the COCO AP protocol for assessing reliability rankings. Experiments on COCO with YOLO-NAS-Pose and YOLO26-Pose show that the learned uncertainty estimates enable keypoint-level reliability ranking, Student-$t$ calibration best captures the empirical residual distribution, and uncertainty-based pruning removes unreliable keypoints. In vision-based aircraft landing, calibrated predictive distributions over runway keypoints support uncertainty-aware position estimation and downstream sensor fusion.

title: MultiWorldBench: Do Independently Controlled Views Describe One Shared World?
summary: Multiplayer world models must ensure that independently controlled views remain consistent with a single shared and persistent world. We introduce MultiWorldBench, a diagnostic Minecraft benchmark comprising 495 case configurations across seven task suites and ten capabilities, including independent control, cross-view motion, shared-state synchronization, persistence, structural reasoning, concurrent interaction, and delayed revisit. Using Engine GT as a reference, we evaluate two multiplayer world models, Solaris (MP) and Gamma-World, together with a single-player generation variant, Solaris (SP). Among the generated systems, Gamma-World achieves the highest ten-capability average at 21.39, followed by Solaris (MP) at 20.88 and Solaris (SP) at 10.06, while Engine GT reaches 91.69. Gamma-World performs better on several control, shared-state, and revisit capabilities, whereas Solaris (MP) leads in cross-view motion and race-condition consistency. Nevertheless, all generated systems score at most 8.00 on state persistence and 1.33 on structural consistency, and none succeeds in spatial reasoning or building-identity preservation. Human pairwise evaluation yields the same overall system ranking and shows strong alignment with the automatic evaluation, with a mean dimension-level Spearman correlation of 0.95. These results show that current multiplayer world models still exhibit a substantial gap relative to Engine GT in maintaining a coherent shared world.
